texts.preamble: Adilakshmamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 11 August, 2025 Kabc020064652022 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore. (Scch-9) Dated This The 11th Day Of August 2025
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident. 2. The brief contents of the petition are as under: On 23.10.2021 at about 10.00 pm., when the petitioner was travelling in a bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 from Vokkaligara Samudhaya Bhavana S.S.Ghati Tobagere Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk near Happy Valley resorts, the driver of the bus drove the same with a very high speed, recklessness and suddenly dashed to the road safety guard at right side but fell down. Due to said impact, the petitioner and other passengers were forcibly knocked down and were sustained multiple grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital Doddaballapura wherein she took treatment as an inpatient for 4 days and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards her treatment and nourishment. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale SCCH - 9 3 MVC No.1075/2022 and healthy and was doing former work and coolie and earning Rs.27,000/- per month. The accident in question occurred due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of Bus bearing reg.No.KA- 06-B-9051 by its driver and the jurisdictional Doddaballapura Rural police have registered a case in their crime No.287/2021, after investigation the said police have filed a charge sheet against the said driver, punishable under Section 279, 338 & 304(A) of IPC. The first respondent being the policy holder and the second respondent being the insurer of said Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- under all heads together with interest and costs. 3. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and respondent No.1 has filed the written statement. SCCH - 9 4 MVC No.1075/2022 4. The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent. Respondent denied the place, date and time of alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner. Respondent contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant. Further denied the involvement of Bus bearing No.KA-06- B-9051 in the alleged accident. Further contended that, driver of the Bus was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident. Further contended that, the said Bus bearing Adilakshmamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 11 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178189769/ 2 reg.No.KA-060B-9051 was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident. Further the respondent No.1 has contended that, the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act. Respondent admitted the issuance of policy of insurance in favour of second respondent in SCCH - 9 5 MVC No.1075/2022 respect of Bus bearing reg.No.KA-06-B-9051 the liability of this respondent company if any is limited to the terms and conditions of the policy. Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.1 prayed to dismiss the petition against it. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked the 10 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10. On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has examined its Legal Officer as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.7 and closed their side evidence.
texts.arguments: The petitioner has contended that due to accident she took treatment at Government Hospital. Moreover, the petitioner has not examined the doctor about assessment of disability. Therefore, the question does not arise to award under the loss of future earning capacity. Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity. f) Towards Deprivation of future Amenities: The petitioner has contended that, on account of the said injuries, she has severe pain, suffering from deep mental shock and agony, very dull due to the accident, cannot sit, squat, stand, walk, climbing stairs and not bear weight etc., As per wound certificate she sustained grevious SCCH - 9 12 MVC No.1075/2022 injury. The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the citation reported in: In (2018) 8 Supreme Court Cases 492 (Rani and others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others) wherein it is held that: " - Defence raised by insurer that offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit to operate in the State concerned - Accepting that defence, High Court absolving the insurer and fastening the liability on the insured i.e., the owner of offending vehicle directing him to satisfy the award - Held, SCCH - 9 14 MVC No.1075/2022 even in such a case, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle - Order of High Court modified accordingly". Civil Appeal No.2253 of 2018 (Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. Tata AIG General Ins. Co., Ltd., and others) wherein it is held that: "Theinsurer, the first respondent herein, opposed the claim on the ground that, the Adilakshmamma vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 11 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178189769/ 6 vehicle in question was driven in violation of the terms of the insurance policy and further the driver was not having a valid and effective driving license and, therefore, it was not obliged to indemnify the insured. That apart, a stand was taken that the vehicle did not have the permit on the date of the accident. On behalf of the owner of the vehicle and driver, assertions were made that the vehicle was insured with the first respondent as per the insurance policy, that the vehicle was registered and the driver had the requisite driving licence.
